semantics.definition:
Returns the variance of each row of the `input` tensor in the given dimension `dim`.

If `keepdim` is `True`, the output tensor is of the same size as `input` except in the dimension(s) `dim`
where it is of size 1. Otherwise, dim is squeezed (see `flow.squeeze()`), resulting in the output
tensor having 1 (or `len(dim)`) fewer dimension(s).

dim.description: the dimension or dimensions to reduce. Defaults to None.
dim.source: dim (int or tuple of ints): the dimension or dimensions to reduce. Defaults to None.

unbiased.description: whether to use Bessel’s correction (:math:`\delta N = 1`). Defaults to True.
unbiased.source: unbiased (bool, optional): whether to use Bessel’s correction (:math:`\delta N = 1`). Defaults to True.

keepdim.description: whether the output tensor has dim retained or not. Defaults to False.
keepdim.source: keepdim (bool, optional): whether the output tensor has dim retained or not. Defaults to False.

variations:

>>> import oneflow as flow

>>> input = flow.tensor(np.random.randn(2, 3, 4, 5))

semantics.definition:
Returns the sum of each row of the ``input`` tensor in the given dimension ``dim`",
treating Not a Numbers (NaNs) as zero. If ``dim`` is a list of dimensions, 
reduce over all of them.

If ``keepdim`` is ``True``, the output tensor is of the same size as ``input`` except 
in the dimension(s) ``dim`` where it is of size 1. 
Otherwise, ``dim`` is squeezed (see :class:`oneflow.squeeze()`), 
resulting in the output tensor having 1 (or ``len(dim)``) fewer dimension(s).

dim.source: dim (int, optional): the dimension to reduce. Default: ``None``

keepdim.description: whether the output tensor has ``dim`` retained or not. Default: `False`
keepdim.source: keepdim (bool, optional): whether the output tensor has ``dim`` retained or not. Default: `False`

dtype.description:
the desired data type of returned tensor. 
            If specified, the input tensor is casted to dtype before the operation is performed.
            This is useful for preventing data type overflows. Default: ``None``.
dtype.source:
dtype (oneflow.dtype, optional): the desired data type of returned tensor. 
            If specified, the input tensor is casted to dtype before the operation is performed.
            This is useful for preventing data type overflows. Default: ``None``.

functionality.scenario: The interface is consistent with PyTorch
variations: The interface is consistent with PyTorch.
functionality.rationale: The interface is consistent with PyTorch.

example.code:
>>> import oneflow as flow
>>> x = flow.tensor([1., 2., float("nan")])
>>> flow.nansum(x)
tensor(3., dtype=oneflow.float32)

>>> x = flow.tensor([[1., float("nan")], [float("nan"), 2]])
>>> flow.nansum(x, dim=1)
tensor([1., 2.], dtype=oneflow.float32)

>>> x = flow.tensor([float("nan") for i in range(3)])
>>> flow.nansum(x)
tensor(0., dtype=oneflow.float32)

semantics.definition:
Applies the Gaussian Error Linear Units function:

.. math:: \text{GELU}(x) = x * \Phi(x)

where :math:`\Phi(x)` is the Cumulative Distribution Function for Gaussian Distribution.

When the approximate argument is 'tanh', Gelu is estimated with:

.. math:: \text{GELU}(x) = 0.5 * x * (1 + \text{Tanh}(\sqrt(2 / \pi) * (x + 0.044715 * x^3)))

approximate.description:
the gelu approximation algorithm to use:
            ``'none'`` | ``'tanh'``. Default: ``'none'``
approximate.source:
approximate (string, optional): the gelu approximation algorithm to use:
            ``'none'`` | ``'tanh'``. Default: ``'none'``

functionality.rationale:

functionality.rationale:

semantics.definition: Returns a tensor with the same size as `input` that is filled with random numbers from a normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1.

input.description: the size of ``input`` will determine size of the output tensor.
input.source: input (oneflow.Tensor): the size of ``input`` will determine size of the output tensor.

dtype.description: The desired data type of returned tensor. defaults to the dtype of `input`.
dtype.source: dtype (flow.dtype, optional): The desired data type of returned tensor. defaults to the dtype of `input`.

generator.description: a pseudorandom number generator for sampling
generator.source: generator (flow.Generator, optional): a pseudorandom number generator for sampling

device.description: The desired device of returned local tensor. If None, defaults to the device of `input`.
device.source: device (flow.device, optional): The desired device of returned local tensor. If None, defaults to the device of `input`.

placement.description:
The desired device of returned global tensor. If None, will
  construct local tensor.
placement.source:
placement (flow.placement, optional): The desired device of returned global tensor. If None, will
  construct local tensor.

sbp.description:
The desired sbp of returned global tensor. It must be equal with the
  numbers of placement, If None, will construct local tensor.
sbp.source:
sbp (flow.sbp, optional): The desired sbp of returned global tensor. It must be equal with the
  numbers of placement, If None, will construct local tensor.

requires_grad.description: If autograd should record operations on the returned tensor. Default: False.
requires_grad.source: requires_grad (bool, optional): If autograd should record operations on the returned tensor. Default: False.

functionality.scenario: Equivalent to specifying shape and type of randn
variations: flow.randn_like(input) is equivalent to flow.randn(input.size(), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device).
functionality.rationale: flow.randn_like(input) is equivalent to flow.randn(input.size(), dtype=input.dtype, device=input.device).

example.code:
>>> import oneflow as flow
>>> x = flow.randn(3,3) # construct local tensor
>>> y = flow.randn_like(x)
>>> y.shape
oneflow.Size([3, 3])
>>> y.is_global
False
>>> placement = flow.placement("cpu", ranks=[0])
>>> sbp = flow.sbp.broadcast
>>> z = flow.randn_like(y, placement=placement, sbp=sbp) # construct global tensor
>>> z.is_global
True

semantics.definition:
Creates a one-dimensional tensor of size :attr:`steps` whose values are evenly
spaced from :math:`{{\text{{base}}}}^{{\text{{start}}}}` to
:math:`{{\text{{base}}}}^{{\text{{end}}}}`, inclusive, on a logarithmic scale
with base :attr:`base`. That is, the values are:

.. math::
    (\text{base}^{\text{start}},
    \text{base}^{(\text{start} + \frac{\text{end} - \text{start}}{ \text{steps} - 1})},
    \ldots,
    \text{base}^{(\text{start} + (\text{steps} - 2) * \frac{\text{end} - \text{start}}{ \text{steps} - 1})},
    \text{base}^{\text{end}})

start.description: the starting value for the set of points
start.source: start (float): the starting value for the set of points

end.description: the ending value for the set of points
end.source: end (float): the ending value for the set of points

steps.source: steps (int): size of the constructed tensor

base.description: base of the logarithm function. Default: ``10.0``.
base.source: base (float, optional): base of the logarithm function. Default: ``10.0``.

dtype.description:
the data type to perform the computation in.
            Default: if None, uses the global default dtype (see oneflow.get_default_dtype())
            when both :attr:`start` and :attr:`end` are real,
            and corresponding complex dtype when either is complex.
dtype.source:
dtype (oneflow._oneflow_internal.dtype = None): the data type to perform the computation in.
            Default: if None, uses the global default dtype (see oneflow.get_default_dtype())
            when both :attr:`start` and :attr:`end` are real,
            and corresponding complex dtype when either is complex.

device.description: the desired device of returned tensor. Default: if None, uses the current device for the default tensor type
device.source: device (Union[str, oneflow._oneflow_internal.device] = None): the desired device of returned tensor. Default: if None, uses the current device for the default tensor type

placement.description: the desired placement of returned global tensor. Default: if None, the returned tensor is local one using the argument `device`.
placement.source: placement (oneflow._oneflow_internal.placement = None): the desired placement of returned global tensor. Default: if None, the returned tensor is local one using the argument `device`.

sbp.description: the desired sbp descriptor of returned global tensor. Default: if None, the returned tensor is local one using the argument `device`.
sbp.source: sbp (Union[oneflow._oneflow_internal.sbp.sbp, List[oneflow._oneflow_internal.sbp.sbp]] = None): the desired sbp descriptor of returned global tensor. Default: if None, the returned tensor is local one using the argument `device`.

requires_grad.description: If autograd should record operations on the returned tensor. Default: False.
requires_grad.source: requires_grad (bool = False): If autograd should record operations on the returned tensor. Default: False.

         [2, 3]]], dtype=oneflow.int64)

semantics.definition:
Applies the element-wise function:

.. math::
    \text{Softplus}(x) = \frac{1}{\beta} * \log(1 + \exp(\beta * x))   

For numerical stability the implementation reverts to the linear function
when :math:`input \times \beta > threshold`.

>>> import oneflow as flow
